name: Early-onset Familial Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension

criteria.description: Presence of clinical signs of portal hypertension (e.g., splenomegaly, variceal bleeding) without evidence of cirrhosis
Liver biopsy showing portal hypertension features without cirrhotic changes
Positive family history of portal hypertension in first-degree relatives
Exclusion of other causes of portal hypertension such as viral hepatitis, alcohol-related liver disease, or schistosomiasis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical portal hypertension without cirrhosis, characteristic liver histopathology, and positive family history) must be met.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of portal hypertension and confirmation by liver biopsy.

occasional.notes: Mild to moderate anemia due to splenic sequestration
Mucosal changes in the stomach due to portal hypertension

rare.notes: Rare due to preserved liver synthetic function
Biliary abnormalities secondary to portal vein obstruction

laboratory: Thrombocytopenia and mild anemia due to hypersplenism
Normal liver function tests or mild elevation of transaminases
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing portal vein enlargement and splenomegaly
Doppler ultrasound excluding portal vein thrombosis initially
genetic: Familial clustering suggests autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Liver biopsy demonstrating portal fibrosis without cirrhosis
Exclusion of viral hepatitis and other liver diseases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cirrhosis on liver biopsy
History of chronic liver disease or risk factors
Serological or stool evidence of schistosomal infection
